176	    // Reserve the notice's byte cost INSIDE maxInlineBytes so the replacement
177	    // (preview + blank line + notice) never exceeds the documented cap — a naive
178	    // preview that spent the whole budget then appended the notice could be
179	    // larger than the cap, and for a marginally-over result even larger than the
180	    // original. The reservation uses a notice priced at the worst-case omission
181	    // count (the full byte total): its digit count bounds the real count's, so
182	    // the reserved size is a safe upper bound and the final notice is never
183	    // longer than what we reserved. `\n\n` is the 2-byte join.
184	    const reserve = Buffer.byteLength(spillNotice({ kind: 'exact', count: totalBytes }, ref), 'utf8') + 2
185	    const previewBudget = Math.max(0, cap - reserve)
186	    const { text: previewText, omitted } = preview(text, previewBudget)
187	    const notice = spillNotice(omitted, ref)
188	    const replacedText = previewText.length > 0 ? `${previewText}\n\n${notice}` : notice
189	    // Invariant: the policy NEVER emits a replacement larger than the cap. When
190	    // the notice alone exceeds maxInlineBytes (a tiny cap or a long spill root),
191	    // there is no within-cap replacement, so keep the inline content — spilling
192	    // would break the advertised cap. (A within-cap replacement is always
193	    // smaller than the original, which is > cap by the entry condition, so this
194	    // one check subsumes "not smaller than the original" too. The spill file
195	    // already written is a harmless orphan; cleanup is deferred.)
196	    if (Buffer.byteLength(replacedText, 'utf8') > cap) {
197	      ctx.logger.warn(`spill-policy: spill notice for ${toolName} exceeds maxInlineBytes; keeping the inline content`)
198	      return undefined
199	    }
